evidence.section: 4.1. Effects of Nb on the phase formation and phase stability
evidence.quote: The HEA with the highest Nb content about 7.2 at.% (i.e., Nb0.25) renders a single BCC and the formation of HCP is completely inhibited.
numerous parallel lath-shaped structures distributed in the matrix appeared (Fig. 6a). The SAD patterns of these areas (Fig. 6b and c) reveal that they have a HCP lattice.

In addition, the SAD patterns (Fig. 6e) of the magnified lath-shaped structure interior (Fig. 6d) reveal existence of the {01 1̄1} twinning spots, which suggests the trace of twinning in the HCP phase.
as the Nb content is decreased, the quantity of dimples, either ellipse or equiaxed, increases but the size decreases, suggesting a more ductile deformation behavior.
Moreover, extensive slip/shear bands were observed inside the grains of alloys Nb0.25, Nb0.2 and Nb0.15, but sparsely in Nb0.
Alloy Nb0.25 shows yield strength of 748 MPa, fracture strength of 843 MPa and ductility of 14.2%.

With further decrease of Nb (i.e., Nb0.15), the tensile curve displays a double yielding behavior, as frequently seen in shape memory alloys. The yield strength is reduced as low as 406 MPa, although the fracture strength is over 1000 MPa.

evidence.section: 4.2. Effects of Nb on the deformation behavior
evidence.quote: The phase transformation process leads to the strong work hardening due to a dynamic strain – stress partitioning effect

In this work, effects of a strong BCC stabilizer, Nb, on crystal structures, phase stability and mechanical properties of the HfNbxTa0.2TiZr (x = 0, 0.15, 0.20 and 0.25) alloys were systematically investigated.
With the increase of Nb, phase constitution exhibits a transition from a nearly single HCP phase (i.e., Nb0) to dual phases of BCC and HCP (hexagonal close packed), i.e., Nb0.15 and Nb0.2.
